ActionDTO.description: ActionDTO describes an action a player can take.

hint.description: Hint is a one-line tooltip (ruleset games). Source says where the action comes from when its button should show it: "book" or "requirement".

impulse.description: Impulse is what the player is asked next, once they have chosen this action.

bot.description: Bot is the id of a built-in bot, from GET /bots.

seat.description: Seat optionally names the open seat the bot takes; without it, the lowest.

AddBotResult.description: AddBotResult is what AddBot reports: the seat the bot took and whether the game started.

bot.description: Bot is the bot's id, as asked for.

name.description: Name is the bot's name at the table, after the seat's faction or colour and its kind (Black Goat (MCTS)).

seat.description: Seat is the seat the bot took.

status.description: Status is the game's afterwards: active when the bot filled the last seat of a game without a lobby, waiting otherwise.

BadgeEventData.description: BadgeEventData is the wire form of a "badge" event.

against.description: Against is how it was earned: "people" or "bots".

game.description: Game is the name of the game it was earned in.

hidden.description: Hidden says the others see it only when the game ends.

BoardDTO.description: BoardDTO describes the board graph and how to draw it.

borders.description: Borders maps region name -> seat color, for tinting board edges.

BotInfo.description: Info describes a registered bot for listings.

BotMatchRequest.description: botMatchRequest is POST /bot-matches' body: two built-in bots to play each other in a two-player game.

bot_a.description: BotA is the bot that plays seat 1: a bot's id from GET /bots.

bot_b.description: BotB is the bot that plays seat 2, also from GET /bots; it may be the same bot as BotA.

delay_ms.description: DelayMS is the pause between moves in milliseconds: 0 or omitted means 700, and a value outside 150..10000 is brought to the nearer end.

game_def_id.description: GameDefID is the game to play, from GET /game-defs; it must have two seats.

BotMatchResponse.description: botMatchResponse is POST /bot-matches' 200 response body: the room the bots play in, to watch as a spectator over /ws/{code}.

room_code.description: RoomCode is the new room's code.

status.description: Status is the game's status: "active", since the bots start at once.

CardBackDef.description: CardBackDef is the back of a card.

CardTypeDTO.description: CardTypeDTO is one kind of card.

CardsDTO.description: CardsDTO is what a client needs to draw the cards of a game: the suits and every card type (the position names cards by id only), what a back looks like and the zones.

standard.description: Standard says the deck can wear a themed set of cards (see card_set on creating a game).

ChatLine.description: ChatLine is one message of a game's chat.

handle.description: Handle is the account that said it, and Guest says a guest did.

server.description: Server says the server wrote it, as it announces a badge (ADR 0130); Seat is then 0.

ClockSnapshot.description: ClockSnapshot is a game clock as clients draw it: one entry per seat, and the seat whose clock is running now (0 when none is).

increment_seconds.description: Increment is the seconds a seat gains each time it hands the turn on.

ConnectionEventData.description: ConnectionEventData is the wire DTO of a "connection" Event.

CounterDTO.description: CounterDTO is a per-seat number kept in a reserve pool.

max.description: Max is the count a win rule wants (Blooms' captures), 0 for none.

also_seats.description: AlsoSeats lists seats, besides Seat, that the creator plays as well (a game against oneself): each is a player of its own, named after the creator and the seat ("Alice · Black Goat").

card_set.description: CardSet draws the cards of a game with a standard deck in a themed set ("amphibians"), for everybody at the table. Omitted: the game's own cards.

clock_increment_seconds.description: ClockIncrementSeconds adds that many seconds to a player's clock each time they hand the turn on. It needs ClockSeconds.

clock_seconds.description: ClockSeconds plays the game with a game clock (a chess clock) instead: a number gives every player that many seconds, a list gives the seats their own times (handicap play). A player whose clock runs out forfeits, or at three seats or more is replaced by a bot. Not for a game of one seat, and not with MoveTimeSeconds.

lobby.description: Lobby makes the game wait, even with every seat filled, until its host starts it (POST /games/{code}/start).

move_time_seconds.description: MoveTimeSeconds optionally limits each move's thinking time; a player who runs out of time loses. Omitted or 0 means untimed.

opponent.description: Opponent optionally names a built-in bot (see GET /bots) that fills the remaining seats so the game starts immediately.

options.description: Options are the game's setup choices (see GET /game-defs/{id}'s "options"): the cults at the table, an expansion. The game created has its own id (base~options), reported by GET /games/{code}.

rated.description: Rated makes the game move its players' ratings when it ends. It takes two accounts, a game of two seats and the same clock for both.

real_time.description: RealTime plays the game in real time; {} takes the default warnings, which only matter in a game with no clock and no time per move.

reserved_seats.description: ReservedSeats keeps open seats for friends ("2": "ana"); InviteOnly keeps the game off every list (ADR 0107).

schedule.description: Schedule sets the game up for later, for accounts (ADR 0109).

seat.description: Seat optionally picks the creator's seat (default 1).

seat_bots.description: SeatBots puts a built-in bot in chosen seats ("2": "random"); seats not listed stay open for people unless Opponent fills them.

seed.description: Seed deals a game of patience (GET /game-defs/{id}: "seeded") from this seed, a whole number: the same seed deals the same cards, so a deal can be played again. Such a game keeps no best score and earns no quick-win badge. Omitted: a new deal.

start_tps.description: StartTPS starts from a TPS position (Tak); StartState from a position document (the "state" object of any observation) with StartSeat moving first. For puzzles, handicaps and "play from here".

CreateGameResponse.description: createGameResponse is POST /games' 200 response body, from session.CreateGameResult.

DealRecord.description: DealRecord is one finished game of patience in an account's deal history.

chosen.description: Chosen says the player chose the deal: it kept no best score.

seed.description: Seed is what the game was dealt from, to play it again.

won.description: Won says the game was won; Moves is the moves it used (state.Moves), which for a win is its score.

DirectCall.description: DirectCall is the wire form of a "dm-call" event: somebody is calling, or a call has ended.

dropped.description: Dropped says the call ended because the person joined another one.

kind.description: Kind is "ring" (this person wants to talk, or has answered) or "end".

DirectCallRequest.description: dmCallRequest is the body of POST /dm/call: ring (or answer) the address To, or hang up with join=false.

DirectHistoryRequest.description: dmReadRequest is the body of POST /dm/history: the correspondence with one person, after the message After (0 for all of it).

DirectHistoryResponse.description: dmHistoryResponse is POST /dm/history's answer: the messages, oldest first.

DirectMessage.description: DirectMessage is one message from one browser to another.

from.description: From and To are addresses; Name is what the sender went by.

DirectMessageRequest.description: dmRequest is the body of POST /dm: a message for the address To.

DirectReadyEventData.description: dmReady is the data of /ws-dm's first event, "ready": the socket is open, and Address is the account's own address.

DirectSignal.description: DirectSignal is the wire form of a "dm-rtc" event: one browser's WebRTC message for another.

DirectSignalRequest.description: dmSignalRequest is the body of POST /dm/signal: one WebRTC message for the person this account is calling.

DirectThread.description: DirectThread is one correspondence, as the list of them shows it.

text.description: Text is the last thing said, and Count how many messages are kept.

with.description: With is the other person's address, and Name what they go by (empty once they have gone).

address.description: Address is the account's own address, the one others write to.

threads.description: Threads are the account's correspondences, newest first.

DirectWebSocketEvent.description: A message the server sends on /ws-dm, a signed-in account's own socket. A client skips an event whose type it does not know.

DisplayDef.description: DisplayDef is the legend of a ruleset game's overlays: what each tint and badge key in the position's view means and how to draw it.

badges.description: Badges are small marks drawn on a cell (a unit's condition).

no_hands.description: NoHands hides the generic reserve ("hand") panels: the ruleset's own view shows what a seat holds.

terms.description: Courts and other named choices a ruleset offers are described in text: key -> one-line description.

tints.description: Tints colours board cells by key (terrain).

ErrorResponse.description: errorResponse is the JSON shape of every error response: {"error": "<message>"}.

FirstMove.description: FirstMove is the deadline for a first move in a real-time tournament's game.

Friend.description: Friend is one line of the friends list.

online.description: Online says they can be seen to be here. CanWrite says a message would reach them: they are online, or are hidden but have themselves written or rung.

FriendInvite.description: FriendInvite is an invitation to a game, as the friends list shows it.

notice.description: Notice is news of the game, shown until dismissed.

FriendRequest.description: friendRequest is the body of the routes about one person or one invitation: POST /friends/request, /answer, /remove, /invite, /invite-answer and /dismiss.

handle.description: Handle is the person's (request, answer, remove, invite).

room.description: Room is the game's room code (invite, invite-answer, dismiss).

FriendSettings.description: FriendSettings is what an account chose about its friends.

accept_invites.description: AcceptInvites says other players may invite the account to games.

FriendsEventData.description: FriendsEventData is the data of /ws-dm's "friends" event, which carries nothing: the friends list changed, and GET /friends reads it again.

FriendsList.description: FriendsList is everything the friends list shows.

GameDef.description: GameDef is one entry of the list of games.

prototype.description: Prototype marks a game whose rules are not final: each version of them is listed as a game of the family, and Version says which.

tutorials.description: Tutorials is how many tutorials a player of this game is offered (see GET /game-defs/{id}/tutorials).

version.description: Version is the game implementation's semantic version; a version below 1.0.0 is a beta.

GameInfo.description: GameInfo is a complete, client-facing description of a game definition: everything a UI needs to draw the board, label the pieces and offer the right actions without parsing position IDs or knowing game-specific rules, and everything an AI client needs to read the rules.

cards.description: Cards describes the suits, card types and zones of a card game.

count_labels.description: CountLabels says what a count selection means after an action.

counters.description: Counters are reserve pools that hold no pieces, only a number per seat (captured stones).

default_clock_minutes.description: DefaultClockMinutes is the time the setup suggests for a game clock, when the game names one (ADR 0081).

display.description: Display is the legend for the tints and badges of a ruleset view.

engine.description: Engine is "ruleset" for games whose rules are written in Go: their moves are a sequence of small decisions, and positions carry a derived view (tints, badges, counters) under state.ext.view.

goals.description: Goals are the regions of the board each seat must connect, as data, so that a client can show each seat's goal in its own way (ADR 0124). Only connect rules are given; win_rules has them all.

guide.description: Guide lists the tabs of the rules window when the game ships its own long-form guide; fetch the pages from /game-defs/{id}/guide.

options.description: Options are the setup choices the game offers its creator (which cults sit at the table, an expansion); send the chosen ones as "options" when creating the game.

params.description: Params are the definition's tunable numbers (victory points needed).

preview.description: Preview is a sample game in play (the squares as in Start.Cells) for games that start with an empty board; absent when the start is picture enough.

sample_view.description: SampleView is a game in progress, in the shape of the state's ext.view, for a game whose table is not a board (state.Sampler).

scores.description: Scores lists tallies worth showing live (e.g. Tak's flats on top).

seeded.description: Seeded says the game is dealt from a seed (ADR 0136): send one as "seed" when creating a game to play that deal again.

setup_catalog.description: SetupCatalog says the setup page draws a picker from GET /game-defs/{id}/setup-catalog.

start.description: Start is the starting position (what a new game looks like), for previews.

version.description: Version is the game's semantic version; Prototype says its rules are not final, and that this game is the version of them that Version names.

view.description: View says the positions carry a derived view under state.ext.view, as a ruleset's do, though the rules are declared: a game of patience (ADR 0122).

GamePersonView.description: GamePersonView is somebody invited, as a page shows them.

answered.description: Answered says they have said which times they can make.

GameReservation.description: GameReservation is a seat kept for a friend, as a page shows it.

GameScheduleView.description: GameScheduleView is a game's schedule, as a page shows it.

GameSlotView.description: GameSlotView is a time offered, as a page shows it.

GameStatusResponse.description: gameStatusResponse is the small answer of the lobby actions: where the game stands after one.

host_seat.description: HostSeat is the host's seat, the one that may start the game and clear other seats; absent in a game without a host.

impulse_seat.description: ImpulseSeat is the seat whose impulse the game waits for, null until it starts.

lobby.description: Lobby is true while the game waits for its host's start.

move_seq.description: MoveSeq is the number of moves played.

status.description: Status is the game's: waiting, active or finished.

Gesture.description: Gesture is one thing a player does in an interface to build a selection: a click on a piece, a square, a count. A client can turn the legal selections into a decision tree keyed by gestures and walk it click by click, so any game's selections are enterable without game-specific UI code. The rules never depend on gestures (ADR 0114).

GetGameResponse.description: getGameResponse is GET /games/{code}'s 200 response body, from session.StateSnapshot — deliberately omits board_state/move_seq, which live at GET /games/{code}/state instead.

clock.description: Clock is the game clock of a game played with one: what each seat has left, and whose clock is running (it counts down from ImpulseDeadline).

draw_offer_seat.description: DrawOfferSeat is the seat offering a draw, or null.

drawn_seats.description: DrawnSeats and AllLost refine a finished game with no winner: the seats that shared a draw (the others lost), or every seat lost.

list_title.description: ListTitle and Tags are what a list of games shows for it, if its rules say.

lobby.description: Lobby: the game waits for its host to start it; HostSeat is the seat of the person who created it. InviteURL is the link that brings a person to the game (the configured public URL, else this server's address).

move_time_seconds.description: Timed games: the per-move allowance, when the player to move runs out of time (RFC 3339) and the server's clock for skew correction.

rated.description: Rated games: what became of the result once the game has ended, and what it did to the players' ratings.

real_time.description: RealTime is set in a game played in real time.

reservations.description: Reservations are the seats kept for friends, and InviteOnly says lists do not show the game.

retired.description: Retired: this server no longer offers the game, GameName is what it was called. The answer is then a record: the seats, the result and move_seq; the moves come from GET .../moves, and nothing else about the game can be asked for or done.

seed.description: Seed is what a game of patience was dealt from, to play the deal again (POST /games: "seed"), from the start. StartChosen says the player chose where the game starts (a seed or a position): it keeps no best score and earns no quick-win badge.

start_state.description: StartState is the position the game began from, present only for games that did not start from the standard position.

tutorial.description: Tutorial is "family/id" of the tutorial the room plays: the page fetches it from GET /game-defs/{family}/tutorials/{id}.

GetGameSeat.description: getGameSeat is one entry of getGameResponse's seats array, from session.SeatInfo.

handle.description: Handle is the account holding the seat, Guest says a guest does, and Yours that it is the asker's own (stage 7 of the accounts plan).

rating.description: Rating is the player's rating, at the seat of a rated game.

replaced.description: Replaced says who held the seat until a bot took it.

GetGameStateResponse.description: getGameStateResponse is GET /games/{code}/state's 200 response body, from session.StateSnapshot. board_state is embedded as a raw JSON object (it's already a JSON string from state.BoardState.MarshalJSON), not a plain string field, so it appears nested rather than doubly-encoded.

board_state.description: BoardState is the v1 flat view (position -> top piece), kept for backwards compatibility; State is the complete position (stacks, reserves, ply) and what new clients should read.

draw_offer_seat.description: DrawOfferSeat is the seat currently offering a draw, or null.

ply.description: Ply is the number of impulses played, which a move's ply guard names.

GoalDTO.description: GoalDTO is one connect rule: regions of the board (in board.regions) that a group of the seat's pieces must join. A client skips a goal whose type it does not know.

of.description: Of and Touch are the regions of a connect goal and how many of them a group must touch, instead of Regions (Havannah's fork: 3 of the 6 sides).

regions.description: Regions are the pairs of regions to connect, any one pair winning.

seat.description: Seat is the seat the goal is for; omitted, it is every seat's.

tag.description: Tag and Piece, when set, say which pieces count: those with the tag, or of that piece type (Tak's road pieces).

type.description: Type is "connect": a connected group of the seat's pieces touches both regions of a pair in Regions, or at least Touch of the regions in Of.

key.description: Key is the guest's key ("bgg_…"), to send as "Authorization: Bearer <key>".

GuideTabInfo.description: GuideTabInfo names one tab of a game's rules guide.

HereRequest.description: hereRequest is POST /here's body: whether the account is here (true by default) or leaving.

HereResponse.description: hereResponse is the answer of /here: who is about, and, to POST, the account's own address.

IndexEndpoint.description: indexEndpoint is one route the index points a newcomer at.

IndexResponse.description: apiIndex is GET /api's body: enough to play a game with curl, and where to read the rest.

docs.description: Docs is where the API's documentation is, and Schema the JSON Schema of its messages (empty when this server has none built in).

version.description: Version is the server's version, which moves with every change to the engine or the platform; APIVersion is the version of the API's messages, whose major a client compares with the one it was built for (ADR 0134).

JoinGameRequest.description: joinGameRequest is POST /games/{code}/join's request body. Role is optional; a blank value defaults to "player" (session.RolePlayer).

seat.description: Seat optionally asks for a particular open seat (a player already at the table keeps theirs).

JoinGameResponse.description: joinGameResponse is POST /games/{code}/join's 200 response body, from session.JoinResult. Seat/Color are tagged omitempty so a spectator's response (Seat == 0, Color == "") genuinely omits those keys rather than sending zero values.

JoinedEventData.description: wsJoined is the data of the "joined" event a game socket starts with.

connected.description: Connected lists the seats that show as connected.

move_seq.description: MoveSeq is the selections played so far: the seq of the last move event.

KickVote.description: KickVote is an open vote as clients see it. Seat is the target's, and Voters holds a seat for each person whose vote counts now.

KickVoteEventData.description: KickVoteEventData is the wire DTO of a "kick_vote" Event: every vote open now.

LegalMoveDTO.description: legalMoveDTO is one selection of GET /games/{code}/selections and simulate.

token.description: Token asks for the session as a token in the answer (SessionTokenResponse) instead of the cookie: a client that is not a browser (ADR 0138).

kind.description: Kind is what the request is now: "anonymous" once signed out, or "guest" when it was not signed in.

MakeMoveRequest.description: makeMoveRequest is POST /games/{code}/moves' request body. A move is given in one of three ways: - legacy: {"from", "to"} (step moves); - structured: {"action", "piece", "from", "to", "count", "path", "drops"} with only the fields the action needs; - notation: {"notation": "3c3>111"} in the game's notation.

ply.description: Ply, when given, is the ply the move was made against: it is refused with 409 if the game has moved on (ADR 0114).

MakeMoveResponse.description: makeMoveResponse is POST /games/{code}/moves' 200 response body, from docs/history/plan.md section 6.8: {"move": {...}, "state": {...}}. State reuses getGameStateResponse's shape. BotMoves lists replies built-in bot opponents played immediately afterwards (already reflected in State).

MeResponse.description: Me is GET /auth/me's answer: who the request comes from.

accounts.description: Accounts says whether this server has accounts at all, and Signup whether a person can make one here.

admin.description: Admin: the account is in the admin group (and may use its powers from here). Mode is "hybrid" or "closed"; SignupMode "open", "invite" or "closed"; Caps what this browser may do.

email.description: Email is the account's own address (never another's).

needs_second_factor.description: NeedsSecondFactor: an administrator without one, off this machine, who may do nothing else until it is set up.

providers.description: Providers are the sign-in providers; Linked those the account signs in with, and Password whether it has one (a provider's account may not).

second_factor.description: SecondFactor says the account signs in with a code too, and RecoveryCodesLeft how many recovery codes it has unused.

Move.description: Move is one move as clients see it: the "move" object of a make-move response, an entry of the move history, and the last move of a game.

auto.description: Auto: the server played the move for a person (a reaction they chose to pass automatically). AutoPlay: a tactical bot played it for a person whose Auto-Play Timeout ran out. Locked: the move rolled dice or drew a hidden token, so nothing can be taken back across it.

ply.description: Ply is the impulse the move is a selection of (ADR 0114).

selections.description: Selections are the parts of a move of several (ADR 0114), in order, each with its own seq (its row); the move itself then has the last one's fields, the notation of all of them joined by "; " and its ply as seq.

MoveEventData.description: MoveEventData is the wire DTO MakeMove publishes as a "move" Event's Data, (docs/history/plan.md section 6.9). It mirrors REST's POST .../moves response shape rather than the raw (untagged) MoveOutcome: BoardState is json.RawMessage so it's sent as a nested JSON object, not double-encoded as an escaped string, and ImpulseSeat is nullable (nil when the move ended the game), matching the convention REST's handleMakeMove already uses for the same reason.

auto.description: Auto: the server played the move for a person (a reaction they chose to pass automatically). AutoPlay: a tactical bot played it for a person whose Auto-Play Timeout ran out.

board_state.description: BoardState is the v1 flat top-of-stack view; State is the full position document (stacks, reserves, ply).

clock.description: Clock is the game clock after the move, for a game played with one.

impulse_deadline.description: ImpulseDeadline is when the next player runs out of time (RFC 3339), and ServerTime the server's clock, for timed games.

locked.description: Locked: the move rolled dice (or drew a hidden token): it cannot be taken back. Sent in a game for one seat only, the one that has Undo.

ply.description: Ply is the impulse this selection is part of (ADR 0114), and EndsImpulse says it ended it: the game's ply is then Ply, else Ply-1.

OKResponse.description: okResponse is the answer of an action that has nothing more to say.

OpenGame.description: OpenGame is one unfinished game as the list shows it.

friends_only.description: FriendsOnly says its seats are all held or kept for friends; ReservedForYou that one is the viewer's. OpenSeats counts only the seats the viewer could sit at.

name.description: Name is the game's name from the catalog ("Hex (11×11)"), and Family the id of the game it is a layout or a derived table of.

players.description: Players are the seats that are taken, people and bots.

seats.description: Seats is how many seats the game has, OpenSeats how many nobody holds.

status.description: Status is "waiting" or "active"; Lobby says it waits for its host.

tags.description: Tags are the short badges the game's rules give it in a list.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is when the game last moved on (a database timestamp).

games.description: Games are the unfinished games, newest change first.

OptionChoice.description: OptionChoice is one value of a seat-choice option.

color.description: Color is the seat color the choice brings with it.

recommended.description: Recommended (a Slot of a book-swap) is the id of the Choice that suits it best.

OptionDef.description: OptionDef is one setup choice of a game, described for clients.

choices.description: Choices are the values of a seat-choice or multi-choice option.

default.description: Default is the value when nothing is chosen: a bool, or for a seat-choice the choice ids per seat.

kind.description: Kind is "bool" (a check box), "seat-choice" (each seat picks one of Choices, no two the same), "multi-choice" (any number of Choices) or "book-swap" (a cult picks one of Choices to replace its Slot).

slots.description: Slots (kind "book-swap") are the things a choice may replace, each in the cult named by its ID: the page offers a Choice for every Slot whose cult is at the table.

OverlayDef.description: OverlayDef is one entry of a DisplayDef legend.

color.description: Color is a CSS color (a hex string).

glyph.description: Glyph is a short text mark (badges).

deals.description: Deals are the asker's finished games of one game of patience, the latest first: the seed each was dealt from and how it went.

Person.description: Person is somebody who is here now.

address.description: Address is where a direct message to them is sent.

since.description: Since is when this browser first said it was here, and Seen when it last did (RFC 3339).

PieceOnBoardDTO.description: PieceOnBoardDTO is one piece on a square.

PlayerRequest.description: playerRequest is the body of the actions that only name the player: undo, resign, start, leave and auto-play-impulse.

PoolDTO.description: PoolDTO describes a reserve pool: a hand of pieces that placed piece types are drawn from.

PositionDTO.description: PositionDTO is one board position with layout coordinates (y grows downwards), and the name and tags of a position that has them (an area of a map: its tags say ocean, land, glyph-dragon…).

ProviderInfo.description: ProviderInfo is a provider as the sign-in page shows it.

RatingChange.description: RatingChange is what a rated game did to the player at a seat.

RealTimeSettings.description: RealTimeSettings is what is chosen at setup, and stored as JSON in games.real_time. The second warning counts from the first. A wait of zero takes its default.

RealTimeSnapshot.description: RealTimeSnapshot is a real-time game's settings as clients see them. Wait is nil when the game is waiting on nobody the warnings apply to.

first_move.description: FirstMove is set while a seat of a real-time tournament's game must make its first move in time, or forfeit.

kick_votes.description: KickVotes are the votes open to have a bot replace a player.

RealTimeWait.description: RealTimeWait says how long the game has been waiting on a person, in a game where that has consequences.

stage.description: Stage is how many warnings have passed: 0, 1 or 2. At 2 the turn is on offer.

ScheduleRequest.description: ScheduleRequest is what a setup asks for: a time or several, and who to invite.

ScoreDTO.description: ScoreDTO describes a running tally: how many squares have a top piece with the given tag (or of the given piece type) owned by each seat.

SeatClock.description: SeatClock is one seat's clock: what it started with and what is left of it (not counting a turn in progress — the seat that is running counts down from the snapshot's ImpulseDeadline).

blend.description: Blend is the two colours a seat is drawn in, when it has two.

colors.description: Colors is every colour the seat plays, when it plays several (ADR 0117): a piece in any of them is the seat's.

SeatEventData.description: SeatEventData is one seat of a StateEventData.

SeatInfo.description: SeatInfo describes one seat a game definition declares: its number, the color it plays, and the name of whoever occupies it ("" if open).

Bot.description: bot ID when a built-in bot plays this seat

Handle.description: Handle is the account's handle when an account holds the seat, and Guest says a guest does (neither: an anonymous client, or nobody).

Name.description: "" if this seat hasn't been filled yet

Rating.description: Rating is the player's rating, at the seat of a rated game.

Replaced.description: Replaced says who held the seat until a bot took it.

SeatRating.description: SeatRating is a player's rating, shown at the seat of a rated game.

SeatReplaced.description: SeatReplaced says who held a seat before a bot took it: they played its moves up to and including move MoveSeq.

SeatReplacedEventData.description: SeatReplacedEventData is the wire DTO of a "seat_replaced" Event.

SeatRequest.description: seatRequest is the body of the lobby's actions on one seat: POST /games/{code}/seat, /remove and /release.

seat.description: Seat is the seat acted on: the open seat to move to, or the seat to clear.

SecondRequest.description: SecondRequest is POST /auth/second's body: a code or a recovery code, and, from a client that is not a browser, the pending sign-in its login answered.

pending.description: Pending is what POST /auth/login answered; with it the answer is a SessionTokenResponse too.

SessionTokenResponse.description: SessionTokenResponse is the answer of a sign-in that asked for a token (ADR 0138): the session, or, when the account has a second factor, the sign-in still to finish. The session is like a browser's (listed, ended by signing out, by ending the other sessions and by a new password, and expiring as a browser's does); its token is sent as "Authorization: Bearer <token>" and needs no X-Bingle-Session.

expires.description: Expires is the latest it lasts; unused for 14 days it ends sooner.

me.description: Me is who is signed in, as GET /auth/me says.

second_factor.description: SecondFactor says the password was right and a code comes next: POST /auth/second with Pending and the code, within five minutes, answers with the session.

token.description: Token is the session's, beginning bgs_.

SlowTurnEventData.description: SlowTurnEventData is the wire DTO of a "slow_turn" Event.

StartDTO.description: StartDTO is a starting position: stacks per square (bottom first) and each color's reserve.

StateEventData.description: StateEventData is the wire DTO of a "state" Event: a full snapshot sent when something other than a move changed the game — a player took a seat ("join"), a move was taken back ("undo") or a player resigned ("resign").

draw_offer_seat.description: DrawOfferSeat is the seat currently offering a draw (null if none).

lobby.description: Lobby: the game waits for its host to start it; HostSeat is the host's seat.

SuitDef.description: SuitDef is one suit: how it is named and drawn.

color.description: Color is a CSS colour for the suit's pips and card faces.

symbol.description: Symbol is the text drawn as the suit's pip (a glyph or a short word).

text.description: Text is a longer description (shown in the rules and on hover).

TournamentRef.description: TournamentRef is what a game says of the tournament it is part of.

WebSocketEvent.description: A message the server sends on /ws/{code}. A client skips an event whose type it does not know.

ZoneDef.description: ZoneDef is a place cards can be.

counts.description: Hidden zones are not shown at all (only their counts, in the seat's panel): useful for a deck.

pile.description: Pile makes the zone a pile: a seat's view lists none of its cards it cannot see, only their count, and a pile a seat holds is not sorted into hand order. How a client draws any zone is its own (ADR 0124: the web page's layouts are in the game's web.yaml).

scope.description: Scope is "seat" (every seat has its own copy: a hand, a trick pile) or "table" (one shared by everyone: the deck, the play area).

visibility.description: Visibility says who sees the faces: "owner" (only the seat the zone belongs to), "all" (everyone; face-down cards still show a back), "flag" (a card is seen by everyone when it is face up and by no one when face down), "none" (no one: a deck, discarded cards).

description: The requests, responses and WebSocket events of bingle's API, version 1.5.0. Generated from the Go types of the server: do not edit. Objects let unknown fields through: a client ignores those it does not know.
